title: Applewood Salmon with Maple-Bavarian Mustard Gravy
description: Applewood scents the poaching broth before maple and Bavarian mustard turn it into a glossy gravy for salmon.

ingredients.name: skinless farmed Atlantic salmon fillet
ingredients.note: Weight after skin and pin bones are removed. Divide into two even portions about 3/4 to 1 inch thick. Fully thaw before cooking.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose unsalted plain meat-and-water broth without a vegetable blend.

ingredients.name: smooth Löwensenf Bavarian mustard
ingredients.note: Pass through a fine sieve first if the mustard contains coarse seeds.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Load the Traeger Silverton 610 with applewood wood pellets. Preheat with the lid closed to 275°F, allowing about 15 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the broth
steps.text: Bring {broth} to a simmer in the small Dutch oven on the stove. Move the uncovered pot to the smoker grate. Close the smoker lid and leave for 12 minutes.

steps.title: Poach under cover
steps.text: Slip {fish} into the hot applewood broth and spoon broth over the tops. Cover the Dutch oven as soon as the salmon goes in. This lid is the wrap from the start.

steps.title: Pull at temperature
steps.text: Keep the Traeger at 275°F. Check from 8 minutes and pull each fillet at 135°F in the thickest center, usually after 10–20 minutes.

steps.title: Rest the salmon
steps.text: Transfer the fish to a warm plate, cover and rest for 3 minutes. Keep the poaching broth in the pot.

steps.title: Season the smoky liquid
steps.text: Pour the hot poaching broth into the HexClad. Whisk in {maple} and {mustard} and bring to a full boil for 1 minute.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish with dill
steps.text: Take the gravy off heat. Swirl in {butter} and {dill} until glossy.

steps.title: Check carryover and doneness
steps.text: After resting, check each thickest center for about 140°F. Open a natural seam with a fork. The center should be opaque and separate easily into flakes. If either cue is unclear or the center is below 140°F, finish covered in hot sauce in the HexClad over low heat to a measured 145°F, checking every minute.

steps.title: Spoon into bowls
steps.text: Place the salmon in two shallow bowls and spoon the mustard gravy between the flakes. Divide the rest of the gravy evenly.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/4 cups for two. Make ahead: Smoke the broth a day ahead while the Traeger is running. Cool promptly, refrigerate, then return it to a simmer before you add the fish. Refrigerate shallow portions within 2 hours, or within 1 hour outdoors above 90°F. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the salmon submerged in its gravy for up to 1 month. A short whisk restores the gravy after thawing. Fridge reheat: Warm a portion covered in its sauce over medium-low heat in the HexClad. Add a little water if it has thickened in storage. Check from 5 minutes and heat to 165°F at the coldest center. Freezer reheat: If frozen, thaw the covered portion in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge method. Option A uses the Bavarian mustard. For gentler Option B, omit it and use a little extra dill with the maple. For dairy-free gravy, omit the finishing butter. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 361 kcal, 30.6 g protein, 9.9 g total carbohydrate, 21.2 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 110 mg sodium. Includes both the fish and its full share of sauce and any rice or potatoes listed. Sodium varies with the broth.
